situation: A fellow team lead, Priya, proposed in our Slack thread that the whole team move from our current tracker, which keeps slowing us down, to a new tool, Trackly, mid-quarter. Our SOC 2 audit evidence lives in the tracker and the audit is Dec 9, so I'd rather pilot Trackly with one squad now and move everyone in January.
reply: Priya, I'm with you on the goal, our current tracker has been slowing us down. Where I land differently is the timing: with the SOC 2 audit on 9 December, I'd rather not move our evidence trail mid-quarter. Could we pilot Trackly with one squad now and move everyone in January? Happy to be told I'm overweighting the audit.
note: A peer's proposal in a public thread: one reason, the strongest, and a pilot that keeps their goal intact.

situation: 老公想把家里30万存款全部拿去买理财，我觉得至少要留8万做应急。想跟他说清楚又不想吵架。
reply: 我明白你是想让钱多赚一点，这个我也想。我这边看法有点不一样：我觉得至少留8万做应急，万一谁工作有变动，不至于手忙脚乱。你是觉得放在理财里也能随时取出来吗？
note: 先认同共同目标，只给一个理由，最后用真诚的问题听他的想法。

situation: My dad and I disagree about electric cars, and he brings it up every time we text. I've told him my view once and don't want to keep going back and forth. We're watching the game together on Sunday.
reply: I don't think we're going to agree on this one, Dad, and that's fine. I'd rather keep things easy between us than win the point. Still on for the game Sunday?
note: When they keep returning to it, you don't have to defend your view again. Saying it once was enough.

situation: 部门群里大家都赞成把周会从周三挪到周一早上8点半，领导也说挺好。我觉得不合适，因为我们组周一上午9点到11点要跟华南区对账，想在群里提议改到周一下午2点。
reply: 周一开会，一周一开始就把重点对齐，这个思路我挺认同的。我这边有一个顾虑：我们组周一上午9点到11点要跟华南区对账，8点半开会很容易跟对账撞上。能不能改到周一下午2点？如果大家觉得早上更合适，我也想听听主要是考虑哪方面。
note: 大家都赞成的方案，先认同目标，只讲自己组的一个具体冲突，给替代时间，再真心问对方的考虑。

situation: Mon associé veut baisser tous nos prix de 20 % pour remplir le carnet de commandes d'ici décembre. On a une petite menuiserie, nos marges tournent autour de 25 %. Je pense que c'est une erreur mais je ne veux pas qu'on se braque.
reply: Je suis d'accord avec toi qu'il faut remplir le carnet de commandes d'ici décembre. Là où je vois les choses autrement, c'est sur les 20 % : avec nos marges autour de 25 %, on travaillerait presque à perte sur chaque chantier. Qu'est-ce qui te fait penser que le prix est le frein principal ? Si tu as eu des retours de clients là-dessus, j'aimerais qu'on les regarde ensemble avant de trancher.
note: Entre associés : d'accord sur l'objectif, le seul chiffre qui compte, puis lui demander ses éléments au lieu d'argumenter.

situation: My mother-in-law Linda, who raised three kids, keeps saying we should put our 4-month-old Leo on his tummy to sleep because 'all my kids were fine'. Our pediatrician, Dr. Shah, said back only, and we swaddle him so he settles. She's babysitting Saturday and I need to text her without starting a war.
reply: Linda, thank you for taking Leo on Saturday, it's a real gift to have you. I know you raised three kids who slept on their tummies and turned out great. Where we land differently is that Dr. Shah was very clear that for Leo it's back only, and we'd feel much better sticking to that for every nap. Is there anything that makes back sleeping tricky for you with him? I'm happy to show you how we swaddle him so he settles.
note: When the point isn't negotiable, aim the curiosity at practical obstacles, not at the rule itself.

situation: GitHub code review. A senior engineer, Sam, commented on my PR asking me to switch our date formatting to moment.js. I think native Intl.DateTimeFormat is better: moment is in maintenance mode and would add about 70 KB minified for the three date formats we use. I don't want to look like I'm fighting a senior dev in a public thread.
reply: Thanks, Sam, and agreed that we want one consistent way to format dates across the app. Where I land differently is the library: I'd lean towards native Intl.DateTimeFormat, mainly because moment is in maintenance mode and would add around 70 KB minified for the three formats we use. Is there a case you have in mind that Intl handles badly? If so, I'm happy to switch, or we can talk it through on a quick call.
note: In a public review thread, the shared goal first, one reason with a number, then a real question that lets the senior person agree or correct you without losing face.

situation: My 17-year-old daughter Ava just told me she's not applying to college this fall; she wants a gap year teaching at a surf school in Portugal. I actually like the gap year idea, I just think she should apply now and defer. She gets defensive fast.
reply: I love that you want to do something real before more school, and honestly I think a gap year could be great for you. Where I land differently is the timing of applications: I'd rather you apply this fall and defer, because doing it now, with your teachers around to help, is much easier than from Portugal next year. What worries you about applying now?
note: With a teenager, agree with the part you genuinely support, disagree on one practical point, and end on a real question instead of a ruling.

situation: I'm on our community garden committee. At last night's meeting everyone liked Frank's idea of spraying weed killer on the paths to save weeding time. The paths run right beside the plots the local school's kids grow food in. I want to post in our committee group chat.
reply: I'm with Frank on the goal, weeding the paths takes far too much of our time. Where I land differently is the spray: the paths run right alongside the school plots, and I'd rather not have weed killer anywhere near beds the kids eat from. Could we try cardboard and wood chips on the two worst paths this month and see if that does the job? If I've missed something about how it would be applied, tell me.
note: Shared goal first, one strong reason, and a small trial instead of a vote against Frank, so he can agree without losing face in the group.

situation: 我妈想把她和我爸住了三十年的老房子卖了，给我和老公凑首付。她说“反正以后也是你们的”。我们俩再攒一年半也能凑够，我不想让他们这么做，但不想让她觉得我不领情。
reply: 妈，我知道您是想让我们早点有自己的家，这份心我特别感激。这件事我想法有点不一样：老房子是您和爸住了三十年的地方，也是你们养老的底，我不想为了首付让你们没了退路。我们俩再攒一年半，首付也能凑够。您是担心房价还会涨吗？
note: 先接住她想帮忙的心意，只讲一个最重要的理由，最后用一个真心的问题了解她的顾虑。

situation: I'm a freelance web designer. My client Marco, who owns an Italian restaurant, wants me to take the prices off the online menu so people 'come in and see'. I think it'll cost him bookings, but it's his call and I want to keep the relationship good. Email.
reply: Hi Marco, I'm with you on the goal, the whole point of the site is getting people through the door. Where I land differently is hiding the prices: in my experience people choosing a restaurant for the first time tend to pick one where they can see what dinner will cost. I could be wrong about your crowd, though. What's behind the change?
note: With a client, disagree once with one reason and a real question, then build what they decide.

situation: My friend Nadia texted that The Salt House, the novel we both read for book club, is the best thing she's read this year, and asked what I thought. I liked the first half, but I found the second half slow, mostly because the sister's storyline just stops. I don't want to dampen her enthusiasm.
reply: I'm so glad it hit you like that, and I liked the first half too. Where I land differently is the second half: I found it slow, mostly because the sister's storyline just stops. What did you make of where she ended up? I might have missed something.
note: Low stakes and they asked: give your view as your view, one reason, and a question that invites them to change your mind.

situation: I manage a design team of five. In today's team meeting Tariq, our junior designer who joined four months ago, proposed redesigning the whole onboarding flow this quarter, with drop-off numbers showing most new users quit during onboarding. I think it's too big with our Nov 20 release, but I don't want to crush his first big idea. Replying in Slack.
reply: Tariq, thanks for bringing the onboarding idea, and I agree the first-run experience is where we lose people; your drop-off numbers made that really clear. Where I land differently is the size of it this quarter: with the 20 November release, I don't think we can do a full redesign well. If you had two weeks, which one screen would you fix first? Sketch that and I'd like to put it on the October plan.
note: When you hold the power, your disagreement lands harder: be specific about what you agree with and turn the no into a smaller yes he can own.

situation: 对门邻居王阿姨提议两家合出钱在楼道口装一道铁门，把我们这头的公共楼道圈起来放鞋柜，每家出1500，她说是为了安全，前阵子楼里丢过快递。物业之前在业主群里说过楼道不能加门、不能堆东西。我们做了十年邻居，关系一直很好。
reply: 王阿姨，您是想让咱们这头更安全、更整齐，这个我特别理解，前阵子楼里丢快递我也挺闹心。我这边想法有点不一样：物业之前在群里说过楼道不让加门、也不让堆东西，真装了万一被要求拆，1500块就白花了。您最担心的是安全，还是东西放不下？要不这周末咱们一起去问问物业有什么办法。
note: 跟老邻居唱反调：先接住她的出发点，理由只讲一个，而且说是物业的要求而不是自己的判断，再一起找替代办法。

situation: Final-round interview for a design lead role on Friday. Last round the design director, Paula, said they're cutting user research entirely to ship faster, and I'm sure she'll ask what I think. At my last job, two days of calls with five users caught a checkout problem that would have cost a full sprint to undo. I disagree with her, but I want the job and don't want to sound preachy. Spoken.
reply: I'm with you on speed; research that holds up shipping can sink a product. Where I land a little differently is cutting research entirely: at my last job, two days of calls with five users caught a checkout problem that would have cost us a full sprint to undo. What's behind the decision, is it mostly time or budget? I may be missing context about how your team works.
note: In an interview, a calm disagreement shows judgement: share the goal, give one real example, then ask so she can add context.

situation: 同期の佐藤さんが部の会議で、来月から全員Excelで日報を出す案を出し、課長は来週決めると言いました。うちのチームはすでにチャットで毎日進捗を共有しているので二重になると思います。会議の場ではなく、佐藤さんに個別にチャットで伝えたいです。
reply: 佐藤さん、会議で出してくれた日報の案について、少し話させてください。チームの進捗を毎日見えるようにしたいという狙いは、私も賛成です。一方で、Excelの日報を別に作ると、今チャットで毎日共有している内容と二重になり、書く手間の割に新しい情報が増えないのではと気になっています。Excelでまとめたい理由があれば、教えてもらえますか。
note: 課長が決める前に本人に個別に伝えれば、皆の前で案を否定された形にならず、相手も案を調整しやすい。

situation: 好朋友阿琳想辞职开奶茶店，打算把攒了五年的20万全投进去，店面选在她家小区门口那条街。那条街上已经有4家奶茶店了。她问我怎么看，我觉得风险太大，但不想泼冷水。
reply: 你想自己干点事，这个我真心支持，也知道这20万是你攒了五年的。我这边的看法有点不一样：那条街上已经有4家奶茶店了，我担心新店很难抢到客人。我不懂这行，也可能想少了。这一点你之前琢磨过吗？要不要先去那几家门口数一个周末的客流再定？
note: 朋友问意见时，一个最强的理由加一个她能自己去验证的问题，比一串风险清单更容易被听进去。

situation: My brother Paul wants to move our mum, 81, into a care home after her fall in August. I think we should first try a carer three mornings a week for two months; her care assessment said she could manage at home with that support. Paul lives nearby and does most of the visiting, and I'd cover the carer's cost and come up every other weekend. I don't want to sound like I'm judging from a distance.
reply: Paul, I know you've carried most of this since Mum's fall, and we want the same thing: for her to be safe. Where I land differently is the next step. Her assessment said she could manage at home with a carer three mornings a week, and I'd like us to try that for two months first, with me covering the carer and coming up every other weekend. What would you need to see in those two months to feel she's okay?
note: Credit the sibling doing the daily work first; if Mum falls and is hurt, call emergency services before anything else.

situation: 我是博士生。导师王老师想让我两周内把论文投出去，赶在年底前有结果。我觉得现在只有一个数据集，审稿人很可能会要求补实验，返修反而更慢。补一组对照实验大概要三周。想在微信上跟他说。
reply: 王老师，我理解您希望这篇文章年底前能有结果，我也想早点投出去。我这边的看法有点不同：现在只有一个数据集，审稿人很可能会要求补实验，到时候返修反而更慢。我想先花三周补一组对照实验再投。您看这样安排是否可行，还是有我没考虑到的地方？
note: 对导师先认同目标，只给一个最强的理由，最后把决定权交回给他。

situation: Mi compañera de piso Irene quiere contratar a una limpiadora cada dos semanas, 60 euros al mes entre las dos. A mí también me agobia cómo está la cocina, pero desde que me bajaron las horas en el trabajo voy justa y prefiero seguir con el cuadrante de limpieza. Se lo quiero decir por WhatsApp sin que se lo tome mal.
reply: Irene, te entiendo, a mí también me agobia cómo está la cocina. Donde lo veo distinto es en lo de la limpiadora: desde que me bajaron las horas voy justa, y 30 euros al mes ahora mismo me pesan. ¿Qué es lo que más te falla del cuadrante? Igual podemos ajustar eso primero y volver a hablar de la limpiadora más adelante.
note: Entre compañeras de piso: primero el objetivo común, una sola razón honesta y una pregunta real sobre qué no funciona.

situation: In today's incident review for last week's outage, my peer Kyle said the root cause was that Jana, our junior engineer, ran the database migration on production without checking. Jana is in the room. I think the real cause is that our deploy script lets anyone run migrations on production without a second approval, and I want to say it out loud without making Kyle look bad.
reply: Kyle, I agree we need to understand exactly how the migration got run, that's the right question. Where I land differently is where the fix sits: our deploy script lets anyone run a migration on production without a second approval, so this could have happened to any of us. Could we make a required second approver the action item? If I'm missing something about how it happened, tell me.
note: Agree with the question, move the disagreement from the person to the process, and hand the room one concrete action.

situation: 爷爷82岁，打算春节自己开车回河北老家，单程四百公里，他说开了五十年车没问题，到了老家用车也方便。上个月他倒车时刮了两次邻居的车。我想周末当面提议这次我来开，但不想伤他面子。
reply: 爷爷，您开了五十年车，这个我一直佩服，也知道您想自己开回去，到了老家用车方便。我这边想法有点不一样：单程四百公里，上个月倒车还刮了两次邻居的车，我担心您路上太累。这次换我来开，您坐副驾帮我看路，您看行吗？要是有我没想到的地方，您跟我说。
note: 跟长辈唱反调：先肯定他的经验，理由只讲他自己经历过的事，再给一个保住他面子的替代办法，最后请他补充。

situation: In our hiring debrief, the hiring manager Laura wants to pass on Omar because he 'wasn't a culture fit', mainly because he was quiet at the team lunch. I ran his technical interview and scored him the strongest of the five candidates. I'm a peer interviewer and want to say this in the meeting without putting Laura on the spot.
reply: Laura, I'm with you that we want someone who'll work well with the team. Where I land differently is on Omar: his technical interview was the strongest of the five candidates, and I'm wary of reading too much into him being quiet at one lunch. What else did you see that made you think he wouldn't fit? I could be missing something.
note: One reason, and a real question; if she holds her view, it's her call as hiring manager.

situation: I'm one of four volunteer moderators on a 3,000-member Discord for indie game devs. Fellow mod Jess wants to permanently ban Ray, who's been helpful there for two years, over one heated post on Tuesday where he called someone's game 'lazy garbage'. Our rules say a first offence gets a warning or a 7-day mute. I'm replying in the private mod channel.
reply: Jess, I'm with you that Ray's post was out of line, and 'lazy garbage' isn't how we want anyone to hear about their game. Where I land differently is the permanent ban: our rules say a first offence gets a warning or a 7-day mute, and I think we should stick to what we've told everyone. Would a 7-day mute plus a note from us explaining why work for you? If there's history with Ray I haven't seen, tell me.
note: Peer to peer, point to the rules you both agreed rather than your view of Ray; the question leaves room for context you don't have.

situation: I'm a hairdresser. My regular client Bea is booked for this Saturday and texted that she wants to go from her dark brown to platinum blonde in one session for a wedding on the 17th. Her hair's been bleached twice this year and snapped at the ends last time, so I'd rather take her to a soft caramel blonde on Saturday and finish the platinum in a second session three weeks later.
reply: Bea, I love that you want to go bold for the wedding, and platinum would really suit you. Where I land differently is doing it all on Saturday: your hair's been bleached twice this year and it snapped at the ends last time, so I'm worried about breakage two weeks before the 17th. Could we take you to a soft caramel blonde on Saturday and finish the platinum in a second session three weeks later? What's drawing you to platinum for this wedding in particular?
note: Your professional judgement is the one reason; the question leaves room for what matters to her before you agree a plan.

situation: 部门同事群里，小刘提议给下个月退休的张师傅凑钱买礼物，每人500元，已经有三四个人回了“好”。我觉得心意到了就行，500元对刚来的几个实习生压力太大，想在群里提议每人随意、上限200元。
reply: 给张师傅送份礼物这个主意特别好，他带了我们这么多年，我也想表示一下。我这边有个小想法：每人500元对刚来的几个实习生可能压力有点大，要不改成每人随意、上限200元？心意到了就好。小刘，你定500元是已经看中了哪件礼物吗？有的话我们一起看看怎么凑。
note: 在群里唱反调：先认同提议本身，只讲一个理由，再问发起人的考虑，给对方留台阶。

situation: My son Theo, 10, swims in a club squad. Coach Danielle announced in the parents' WhatsApp group that from November the squad trains five mornings a week at 6am instead of three. Theo is already worn out on the three early mornings, and I'd like him to stay on three; I want to message her privately, not in the group.
reply: Hi Danielle, thanks for all the work you put into the squad, and I can see the extra sessions are about helping the kids improve. Where I land differently is for Theo: he's already worn out on three 6am mornings, and I'd rather he stayed on three for now. Could that work within the squad, or is five a requirement? I'd also like to hear what you're seeing in the pool that I might not be.
note: Parent to coach: disagree only about your own child, in private, and leave room for what she sees at training.

situation: My best friend Josh is planning to propose to his girlfriend Amira at her company's 200-person Christmas party on Friday 18 December, with a flash mob, and he asked what I think. Amira told me last year she'd hate a public proposal because being the centre of attention makes her anxious.
reply: I love that you want to make it a big, joyful moment, and I'm so happy for you both. Here's where I land differently: I'd make it private. Last year Amira told me she'd hate a public proposal, because being the centre of attention makes her anxious. What drew you to the party idea? If you want, I'll help you plan a private version.
note: Lead with the one reason that is hers, not your taste, and leave the decision with him.

situation: 家族微信群里，68岁的舅舅转了一篇文章，说每天喝芹菜汁能代替降压药，还说他自己已经停药一周了。舅舅有高血压。我不想在群里当众反驳他，想私聊。
reply: 舅舅，看到您在群里转的芹菜汁那篇文章了。您想用更天然的办法把血压管好，这个我特别理解，谁都不想一直吃药。我这边想法有点不一样：我担心的是没跟医生商量就把药停了。您停药这一周量过血压吗？要不这周我陪您去趟医院，问问医生怎么调整。
note: 长辈的健康问题私聊说，只讲一个担心、不争文章对错；如果他出现剧烈头痛、胸痛或说话不清，马上打120。

situation: Yesterday on Slack I told my co-founder Mei I'd rather not hire a second salesperson until we reach 40 paying customers; we're at 28. She replied 'So you think my plan is wrong?' and went quiet. We have our usual Monday check-in, and I want to reply now without backing down or making it bigger.
reply: Not wrong, Mei. We want the same thing, more revenue sooner, and where we differ is only the timing: I'd still rather wait until we're at 40 customers, from the 28 we have now. Could we use Monday's check-in to agree the number that would make us both comfortable hiring? I'd rather decide this together than be right about it.
note: When disagreement lands as an attack, separate the idea from the person once, then move from who is right to how you'll decide.

situation: My co-author Dr. Wei Lin, who is senior to me, wants the abstract of our paper to say that night-shift work 'causes' poor sleep in nurses. Our study is a one-time survey of 412 nurses, so I'd rather write 'is associated with'. I'm leaving a comment in our shared draft.
reply: Wei, I agree the night-shift finding is the heart of the paper and belongs front and centre in the abstract. Where I land differently is the word 'causes': with a one-time survey of 412 nurses, I think reviewers will push back on a causal claim, so I'd suggest 'is associated with'. Is there something in the data you're seeing that supports the stronger wording? Happy to be corrected.
note: In a shared draft, comment on the wording, not the person; if you still differ after her answer, agree who makes the final call.

situation: 老公想给6岁的儿子乐乐报四个兴趣班：周六上午游泳、下午英语，周日上午围棋、下午画画，他是想让孩子多学点东西。我觉得这学期最多报两个，因为乐乐这两周已经说了好几次“周末好累，想在家玩”。今晚想跟他商量。
reply: 我知道你是想让乐乐多学点东西，以后路宽一些，这个我也想。我这边看法有点不一样：我觉得这学期最多报两个。乐乐这两周已经说了好几次“周末好累，想在家玩”，四个班把周末全排满，我怕他还没学进去就先烦了。你觉得四个里面哪两个对他最重要？我们一起挑。
note: 跟伴侣在孩子的事上唱反调：先认同目标，理由用孩子自己说过的话，再把否决变成一起挑选。

situation: A stranger in my industry, Martin Reyes, posted on LinkedIn that 'remote work is killing junior developers' growth', and it's getting a lot of agreement. I've mentored four junior engineers fully remotely over the last three years, with a daily 30-minute pairing session, and three of them were promoted within 18 months. I want to comment publicly without starting a pile-on.
reply: Agree that juniors need a lot of real time with experienced people, Martin; that's what makes or breaks the first year. Where I land differently is 'killing'. I've mentored four junior engineers fully remotely over the last three years, with a daily 30-minute pairing session, and three of them were promoted within 18 months. What have you seen go wrong most often?
note: In public with a stranger: one piece of your own evidence and a real question; if he pushes back, one reply at most, then leave it.

situation: My co-host Dev wants our comedy podcast to take a $600-an-episode sponsorship from SpinLuck, a sports betting app. I agree we need money for new mics, but a lot of our listeners have written in about recovering from gambling debt, and I don't want to read betting ads to them. We record on Thursday.
reply: Dev, I'm with you that we need the money, and $600 an episode would sort the new mics fast. Where I land differently is SpinLuck: a lot of our listeners have written in about recovering from gambling debt, and I'm not comfortable reading betting ads to them. What drew you to this one in particular? I'd like us to settle it together before Thursday's recording.
note: The one reason is about the listeners, not Dev's judgement; if you still differ, agree how the two of you decide on sponsors.

situation: In our friends' group chat, Kat wrote that Lena is 'obviously only with Tom for his money'. I don't think that's fair: Lena kept working two jobs while Tom was out of work for most of last year. Kat has known Tom since school and is protective of him; Lena isn't in the chat, and I want to push back without starting a fight.
reply: I'd gently push back on that one, Kat. I know you've had Tom's back since school, and that's a good thing. I see Lena differently: she kept working two jobs while Tom was out of work for most of last year. Has something happened that I don't know about?
note: Defending someone who isn't there: one fact you know first-hand, no attack on Kat, and if she digs in, say you see it differently and leave it.

situation: On Thursday our team debated moving the product launch from November to January, and our manager, Lucy, made January final. I argued for November because our two biggest customers, Halden and Marlow, asked for the feature before their year-end; I lost. I want to post in our team Slack that I still see it differently but I'm fully behind January.
reply: Now that January's final: I'm with everyone on wanting a launch we're proud of, and that's what the extra time buys us. For the record, I still see it a little differently, mainly because Halden and Marlow asked for the feature before their year-end. I've said my piece, and I'm fully behind January. If anyone has ideas for keeping those two happy in the meantime, I'm all ears.
note: Once the call is made, say your view once for the record, then commit out loud; don't reopen it in the thread.

situation: 我爸想按族谱给我刚出生的儿子取名“王承祖”，“承”是我们家的字辈。我和老婆一直喜欢“一然”，我们想要一个轻快些的名字，商量好最后由我们俩定，但也想尊重字辈。周六回家想当面跟我爸说，提议叫“王承然”。
reply: 爸，您想按族谱给孩子取名，让他记得自己是“承”字辈的，这份心意我们俩特别看重。名字这件事我们想法有点不一样：我们一直喜欢“一然”，想给孩子一个轻快些的名字。要不叫“王承然”，字辈留着，也有我们喜欢的那个“然”？您觉得这个名字怎么样？
note: 跟长辈唱反调：先接住字辈背后的心意，只讲一个理由，给一个保留字辈的方案，再真心问他怎么看。

situation: 老公想这个月就去领养一只金毛幼犬，说儿子盼了很久。我也想养狗，但我们现在租的两居室，租房合同里写着不许养宠物，明年三月就搬去带院子的新房。我想等搬家后再养，这之前周末可以先带儿子去救助站做志愿者。
reply: 我知道你是想让儿子早点有只狗陪着，这个我也盼着。我这边想法有点不一样：我想等明年三月搬家以后再养，现在的租房合同写着不许养宠物，万一被房东发现就麻烦了。你是担心儿子等不了那么久吗？这之前周末我们可以先带他去救助站做志愿者，跟狗狗多处处。
note: 理由用合同里写明的条款，而不是自己的偏好；具体能不能养，以合同原文和房东的答复为准。
